bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds utilized to strengthen balance sheet (Net Worth up to INR 2,809mn); Priority on funding working capital cycle (receivables days extended) to retain/grow customers; No dividends mentioned, focus on retained earnings for growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global trade volume slowdown; Inventory correction in key markets (US/Europe); Dependency on Asia region (85% of TEUs); Working capital strain from extended credit periods (Receivables up 70%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges macro headwinds (rates/volumes) but emphasizes strategic customer retention via credit extension and diversification success; Confident in FY27 recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Significant increase in 'Other Current Assets' driven by prepayments to shipping lines ahead of customer invoicing (15-20 day lag), indicating active management of carrier relationships to secure capacity/pricing despite volume headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Debt-to-Equity ratio at 0.18x in FY2026, indicating a strong balance sheet position'.
- Returns for FY26 are stated inconsistently within the deck: the Key Facts slide shows '19.9% FY26 ROE' and '18.8% FY26 ROCE', while the investment-case slide states 'Return on Equity of 19.9% and Return on Capital Employed of 20.9% in FY2026'. Both ROCE readings are recorded as printed.
- FY26 headline scale as printed: INR 7,226 Mn FY26 Revenue, INR 495 Mn FY26 EBITDA, INR 377 Mn FY26 PAT, with 'EBITDA margin of 6.9% and PAT margin of 5.2% in FY2026, improved through operational and cost efficiency'.
- 'Revenue CAGR of 14.7% over FY2023-FY2026, highlighting consistent growth potential' (deck-stated).
- The deck states no dividend policy, payout ratio, buyback or explicit reinvestment/capital-allocation framework.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- customer lock-in: deep-rooted Asia trade network with long-standing relationships across China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand — evidence: anchors around 85% of Fiscal 2026 revenue
- distribution: PAN-India network with owned infrastructure headquartered in Chennai, one of India's major port hubs — evidence: operates through a network of 8 branch offices covering major transportation hubs
- customer lock-in: high customer stickiness with growing repeat-customer base — evidence: repeat customers grew from 871 to 959 during the year, with the top five customers holding a stable ~33% revenue share
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Freight rate cyclicality and spread compression — Revenue and forwarding spreads are geared to the container rate cycle, as Fiscal 2026 demonstrated.
- Trade-policy and geopolitical disruption — Tariff measures, import-policy changes on Southeast Asia corridors and conflict-driven rerouting can alter flows with little notice.
- Customer concentration — Top five customers contributed approximately 33% of revenue.
- Vertical concentration in renewable energy — Renewable energy represented 40.9% of Fiscal 2026 revenue; import mix is shifting with domestic manufacturing localisation and policy-sensitive demand.
- Execution risk on the asset-ownership transition — Capital deployment, driver availability/training, fleet utilisation and operating capability must scale together.
- Working capital and receivables intensity — Receivables increased approximately 60% on extended credit days; the business model also requires structural early payment to shipping lines and agents ahead of customer invoicing.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Sea Import: 78% of FY26 revenue (dominant vertical); Sea Export: 14% of FY26 revenue (improved traction); Air Import: 2.4% of revenue (+23.6% YoY); Air Export: 1.2% of revenue (>100% YoY growth); Road: ~5% of revenue.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Soft freight rates and global inventory correction reducing shipment volumes | Pure-play volume-dependent logistics peers | loser | Med | Companies without Glottis's diversification into high-growth verticals (Auto/Agro) or strong Asia focus may face steeper revenue declines. |
| Rising working capital requirements due to extended credit days | Small unlisted freight forwarders | loser | High | Lack of IPO capital prevents smaller players from extending credit to retain customers, potentially losing market share to funded listed entities like Glottis. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- 'Over two decades of providing end-to-end Logistics Services' across Ocean Freight, Air Freight and Land Transport, plus ancillary General Warehousing, Cross Docking, 3PL Services and Custom Broking.
- FY26 Revenue mix by mode as labelled on the deck: 'Ocean Freight - 92%', 'Inland Transportation - 5%', 'Air Freight - 3%' of INR 7,226 Mn FY26 Revenue.
- Renewable-energy logistics is the stated moat: 'Leading logistics partner for India's renewable energy imports and exports, managing a significant share of solar sector cargo movement', with 'Expertise in handling logistics for solar panels, solar cells, glass panels, and solar manufacturing equipment'.
- 'Headquartered in Chennai, one of India's major port hubs'; operates PAN-India through 9 branch offices (Gandhidham, Kolkata, Mumbai, Tuticorin, Coimbatore, Bengaluru, Cochin, New Delhi, Ahmedabad) with regional offices in Singapore, the UAE and Vietnam. FY26 Revenue Mix shown as India 87% / International 13%.
- Recognitions cited: 'Freight Forwarder of the Year (Imports)' 2022, 2023 and 2024, 'Freight Forwarder of the Year (Containerized)' 2019, and approval as a member of the International Federation of Freight Forwarders Association in 2024.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Credit rating] CRISIL 'BBB+/Stable' as of July 2026.
- [Customer concentration] 'Top 5 Customers Revenue Contribution 29%' for Q1 FY27; management notes 260 new customers were added in the quarter and that top-five contribution 'reduced to 29% of revenue'.
- [Volume vs realisation] Management states shipment volumes 'remained lower' while revenue rose, attributing the increase to 'higher realizations' - so revenue growth and TEU growth diverge in this deck; freight-rate movement across trade corridors is named as a swing factor.
- [Industry data source] Market context is sourced to a 'Freight Forwarding Industry report' dated August 31, 2025 prepared and issued by 1Lattice; it projects renewable (solar) installed capacity growing 'at 23.8% CAGR during FY25-30, supported by India's target to reduce carbon intensity by < 45 % by 2030'.
- [Two Managing Directors] The Board of Directors slide lists both Ramkumar Senthilvel and Kuttappan Manikandan with the designation 'Managing Director', alongside one Non-Executive Director and three Independent Directors.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Founded in 2004 and headquartered in Chennai, Glottis is an integrated logistics and supply chain partner offering ocean freight (FCL/LCL), air freight, road transportation, warehousing, customs broking, cross-docking and 3PL services. It serves a diversified customer base across renewable energy, engineering products, granite and minerals, textiles, automobiles, agro products, chemicals, timber, medical products and consumer goods, connecting Indian exporters/importers to global trade corridors through an outsourcing-led, asset-light operating model complemented by a growing owned vehicle fleet.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Freight and Forwarding Services:** Ocean Freight (FCL/LCL), Air Freight, Land Transport / Road Transportation
- **Warehousing and Value-Added Services:** General Warehousing, Cross Docking, 3PL Services, Customs Broking

- distribution: PAN-India network with owned infrastructure headquartered in Chennai, one of India's major port hubs — evidence: operates through a network of 8 branch offices covering major transportation hubs
- customer lock-in: high customer stickiness with growing repeat-customer base — evidence: repeat customers grew from 871 to 959 during the year, with the top five customers holding a stable ~33% revenue share
business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed slightly in Q4 (5.4%) vs FY26 average (6.9%) due to mix/rates; Cost structure flexible as bunker/fuel fluctuations (BAF) are fully passed through to customers, neutralizing oil price volatility impact on margins.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Positive outlook for FY27 to recover FY26 declines; Margin: Focus on operational discipline to maintain ~6-7% EBITDA; Order inflow: Targeting new customer acquisition (163 added in FY26); Capex/commissioning: Selective network expansion, no heavy capex mentioned.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - Business operates on transactional shipment basis without a traditional multi-year order book; visibility tied to monthly TEU throughput.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Diversification into Automobile (revenue share doubled to 4.2%) and Agro products (+58.7% YoY); Geographic expansion in inter-Asia trade routes; Increasing wallet share with top 5 customers (stable at 33%) while broadening base to 959 repeat customers.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Selective asset ownership / backward integration: transitioning core lanes from hired to owned assets (trailers, containers) to improve cost control, service reliability and margin capture
- Vertical diversification: building on renewable-energy leadership (including the emerging BESS/energy-storage opportunity) while scaling automobiles, agro products, engineering, pharmaceuticals and other identified verticals
- Service-line completion: deepening ocean export, air freight, road transport, warehousing and 3PL to move from freight forwarder to total logistics provider
- Geographic expansion: new wholly owned foreign subsidiary in the United States, alongside existing entities in Singapore, the UAE and Vietnam, and export-corridor development into Cambodia, Africa, China and Europe
- Sales and organisational build-out: new sales teams commissioned in western and northern India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, National Capital Region) to reduce historical concentration of origination in southern India
- Expanding beyond the traditional southern-India stronghold into northern and western India for deeper customer engagement and broader market access
- Advancing technology capabilities through digital platforms, specialised ERP solutions, freight process automation and real-time operational visibility
- Aligning growth with government infrastructure initiatives (PM-KUSUM, PM Suryodaya, Make in India, Bharatmala, Gati Shakti, Sagarmala)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Glottis is executing a phased 'backward integration' asset-ownership programme: the owned commercial-vehicle fleet expanded from 17 to 42 vehicles during Fiscal 2026, within a broader programme of approximately 150 trailers and approximately 1,000 containers. Orders for approximately 1,000 containers were initiated in Q4 FY26, with the containers expected to enter service from Q1 FY27. Trailer purchases are being executed in multiple tranches aligned with driver availability and training (each batch of drivers undergoes one to two weeks of training before vehicles are commissioned). The Company opened a new branch in Ahmedabad during Q3 FY26 (its second in Gujarat alongside Gandhidham), taking the domestic branch network to nine offices. During the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Glottis Inc., in Texas, USA (March 2026), and the Board approved incorporation of another wholly owned subsidiary in Malaysia (incorporation underway as at March 31, 2026), complementing existing group entities in Singapore, the UAE and Vietnam.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management's plans do not depend on a freight-rate recovery; they depend on volume growth, mix improvement and cost capture, each within the Company's influence
- Backward-integration economics (higher-margin owned-trailer transport revenue and lower container vendor costs) are expected to flow through as the trailer programme completes and approximately 1,000 owned containers are commissioned from Q1 FY27
- Scaling of emerging cargo categories where the Company has early positions — battery energy storage systems, raw materials and capital equipment for India's expanding solar manufacturing capacity, and automobile logistics under recently signed contracts
- Continued growth in ocean export, air freight and road transport share, and operationalising the United States subsidiary
- Medium-term ambition of progressive EBITDA margin improvement towards double digits, driven by owned-asset economics, operating leverage from the expanded network and normalisation of the rate environment
- Competitive advantage in the fragmented Indian freight-forwarding market accrues to players with scale relationships with shipping lines, sector specialisation, balanced asset ownership and balance-sheet strength to invest through downturns
- Renewable energy transition redefined: raw-material imports for domestic module manufacturing, BESS/energy-storage container movements (early entrant with signed contracts) and capital-equipment flows into India are enlarging the renewable logistics task even as finished-module imports decline
- Vertical diversification showing demonstrated traction: automobile revenue more than doubled during Fiscal 2026 to 4.2% of revenue from 1.5%; agro products grew to 5.7% of revenue from 2.8%, with identified pipelines in chemicals, textiles, pharmaceuticals and medical products
- Service-line diversification: air import revenue grew 23.6% and air export more than doubled; ocean export share rose to approximately 14% of revenue
- Asset ownership as a margin lever: management estimates owned trailers can yield EBITDA margins of 15-20% on associated transport revenue, and owned containers can reduce related vendor costs by approximately 20-22% from existing levels
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Glottis reported a resilient Q4 with sequential revenue growth (+36% QoQ) and strong profitability (5.4% EBITDA margin) despite a full-year revenue decline driven by soft freight rates and lower global volumes. The company leveraged IPO proceeds to turn net cash positive (INR 510mn) while strategically extending credit terms to capture market share, signaling a shift from pure volume defense to aggressive relationship-based expansion.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Glottis is an asset-light, integrated multimodal logistics and freight-forwarding partner spanning ocean, air and road transportation, with a specialised leadership position in renewable-energy (solar) logistics.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Founded in 2004 and headquartered in Chennai, Glottis is an integrated logistics and supply chain partner offering ocean freight (FCL/LCL), air freight, road transportation, warehousing, customs broking, cross-docking and 3PL services. It serves a diversified customer base across renewable energy, engineering products, granite and minerals, textiles, automobiles, agro products, chemicals, timber, medical products and consumer goods, connecting Indian exporters/importers to global trade corridors through an outsourcing-led, asset-light operating model complemented by a growing owned vehicle fleet.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Glottis Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Texas, United States on 18 March 2026; 100% shareholding.
- Glottis (Malaysia) — proposed subsidiary — subsidiary: Board approved incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Malaysia on 19 March 2026 to expand international presence; incorporation was underway as on 31 March 2026.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Sea Import: 78% of FY26 revenue (dominant vertical); Sea Export: 14% of FY26 revenue (improved traction); Air Import: 2.4% of revenue (+23.6% YoY); Air Export: 1.2% of revenue (>100% YoY growth); Road: ~5% of revenue.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Freight and Forwarding Services:** Ocean Freight (FCL/LCL), Air Freight, Land Transport / Road Transportation
- **Warehousing and Value-Added Services:** General Warehousing, Cross Docking, 3PL Services, Customs Broking

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A - Business operates on transactional shipment basis without a traditional multi-year order book; visibility tied to monthly TEU throughput.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: Positive outlook for FY27 to recover FY26 declines; Margin: Focus on operational discipline to maintain ~6-7% EBITDA; Order inflow: Targeting new customer acquisition (163 added in FY26); Capex/commissioning: Selective network expansion, no heavy capex mentioned.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Diversification into Automobile (revenue share doubled to 4.2%) and Agro products (+58.7% YoY); Geographic expansion in inter-Asia trade routes; Increasing wallet share with top 5 customers (stable at 33%) while broadening base to 959 repeat customers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management's plans do not depend on a freight-rate recovery; they depend on volume growth, mix improvement and cost capture, each within the Company's influence
- Backward-integration economics (higher-margin owned-trailer transport revenue and lower container vendor costs) are expected to flow through as the trailer programme completes and approximately 1,000 owned containers are commissioned from Q1 FY27
- Scaling of emerging cargo categories where the Company has early positions — battery energy storage systems, raw materials and capital equipment for India's expanding solar manufacturing capacity, and automobile logistics under recently signed contracts
- Continued growth in ocean export, air freight and road transport share, and operationalising the United States subsidiary
- Medium-term ambition of progressive EBITDA margin improvement towards double digits, driven by owned-asset economics, operating leverage from the expanded network and normalisation of the rate environment
- Competitive advantage in the fragmented Indian freight-forwarding market accrues to players with scale relationships with shipping lines, sector specialisation, balanced asset ownership and balance-sheet strength to invest through downturns
- Renewable energy transition redefined: raw-material imports for domestic module manufacturing, BESS/energy-storage container movements (early entrant with signed contracts) and capital-equipment flows into India are enlarging the renewable logistics task even as finished-module imports decline
- Vertical diversification showing demonstrated traction: automobile revenue more than doubled during Fiscal 2026 to 4.2% of revenue from 1.5%; agro products grew to 5.7% of revenue from 2.8%, with identified pipelines in chemicals, textiles, pharmaceuticals and medical products
- Service-line diversification: air import revenue grew 23.6% and air export more than doubled; ocean export share rose to approximately 14% of revenue
- Asset ownership as a margin lever: management estimates owned trailers can yield EBITDA margins of 15-20% on associated transport revenue, and owned containers can reduce related vendor costs by approximately 20-22% from existing levels

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin compressed slightly in Q4 (5.4%) vs FY26 average (6.9%) due to mix/rates; Cost structure flexible as bunker/fuel fluctuations (BAF) are fully passed through to customers, neutralizing oil price volatility impact on margins.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds utilized to strengthen balance sheet (Net Worth up to INR 2,809mn); Priority on funding working capital cycle (receivables days extended) to retain/grow customers; No dividends mentioned, focus on retained earnings for growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Glottis is executing a phased 'backward integration' asset-ownership programme: the owned commercial-vehicle fleet expanded from 17 to 42 vehicles during Fiscal 2026, within a broader programme of approximately 150 trailers and approximately 1,000 containers. Orders for approximately 1,000 containers were initiated in Q4 FY26, with the containers expected to enter service from Q1 FY27. Trailer purchases are being executed in multiple tranches aligned with driver availability and training (each batch of drivers undergoes one to two weeks of training before vehicles are commissioned). The Company opened a new branch in Ahmedabad during Q3 FY26 (its second in Gujarat alongside Gandhidham), taking the domestic branch network to nine offices. During the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Glottis Inc., in Texas, USA (March 2026), and the Board approved incorporation of another wholly owned subsidiary in Malaysia (incorporation underway as at March 31, 2026), complementing existing group entities in Singapore, the UAE and Vietnam.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges macro headwinds (rates/volumes) but emphasizes strategic customer retention via credit extension and diversification success; Confident in FY27 recovery.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- customer lock-in: deep-rooted Asia trade network with long-standing relationships across China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand — evidence: anchors around 85% of Fiscal 2026 revenue
- distribution: PAN-India network with owned infrastructure headquartered in Chennai, one of India's major port hubs — evidence: operates through a network of 8 branch offices covering major transportation hubs
- customer lock-in: high customer stickiness with growing repeat-customer base — evidence: repeat customers grew from 871 to 959 during the year, with the top five customers holding a stable ~33% revenue share

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Global trade volume slowdown; Inventory correction in key markets (US/Europe); Dependency on Asia region (85% of TEUs); Working capital strain from extended credit periods (Receivables up 70%).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Significant increase in 'Other Current Assets' driven by prepayments to shipping lines ahead of customer invoicing (15-20 day lag), indicating active management of carrier relationships to secure capacity/pricing despite volume headwinds.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Selective asset ownership / backward integration: transitioning core lanes from hired to owned assets (trailers, containers) to improve cost control, service reliability and margin capture
- Vertical diversification: building on renewable-energy leadership (including the emerging BESS/energy-storage opportunity) while scaling automobiles, agro products, engineering, pharmaceuticals and other identified verticals
- Service-line completion: deepening ocean export, air freight, road transport, warehousing and 3PL to move from freight forwarder to total logistics provider
- Geographic expansion: new …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Credit rating] CRISIL 'BBB+/Stable' as of July 2026.
- [Customer concentration] 'Top 5 Customers Revenue Contribution 29%' for Q1 FY27; management notes 260 new customers were added in the quarter and that top-five contribution 'reduced to 29% of revenue'.
- [Volume vs realisation] Management states shipment volumes 'remained lower' while revenue rose, attributing the increase to 'higher realizations' - so revenue growth and TEU growth diverge in this deck; freight-rate movement across trade corridors is named as a swing factor.
- [Industry data source] Market context is sourced to a 'Freight Forwarding Industry report' dated August 31, 2025 prepared and issued by 1Lattice; it projects renewable (solar) installed capacity growing 'at 23.8% CAGR during FY25-30, supported by India's target to reduce carbon intensity by < 45 % by 2030'.
- [Two Managing Directors] The Board of Directors slide lists both Ramkumar Senthilvel and Kuttappan Manikandan with the designation 'Managing Director', alongside one Non-Executive Director and three Independent Directors.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
